papers.title: ResWAM: Learning What Changes, Not What Stays, for World-Action Models
papers.problem: Robot models that predict future frames waste effort copying static background, and they need heavy compute.
papers.fix: A small model that learns only what changes between frames reached 81.1% on LIBERO-Plus and 93.8% on RoboTwin 2.0.
papers.practicalUseCase: If change-only training works, robot makers can cut compute; train on motion differences instead of full future frames.
papers.limitation: Tests ran without robot pretraining, and real-robot results cover only three tasks: Open, Put, and Stack.

papers.title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers
papers.problem: People who let an AI write model weights by hand kept the Transformer design without asking if it fits.
papers.fix: Three AI models chose lookup tables, hitting up to 54.4% accuracy with about 1,800x fewer parameters than a Transformer.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you write weights by hand, use a table you can read and fix row by row, not a Transformer.
papers.limitation: Pretrained language models stay more accurate; the claim covers only which structure to build when writing weights.

papers.title: Multi-Branch Transformer
papers.problem: Language models grow only by getting wider or deeper, which raises training cost and slows long-text decoding.
papers.fix: Running blocks in parallel branches cut KV-cache storage by up to 34% and raised decoding speed by up to 51.4%.
papers.practicalUseCase: Standard Transformers need up to 1.26x more training compute to match branched models, so test branches before widening models.
papers.limitation: Tests used models of only 0.8B to 2.1B total parameters, so larger sizes remain unproven.

papers.title: MedJev: A System One Vision-Language Decision Model for Fast and Effective Medical Image Understanding
papers.problem: Medical image AI writes long reasoning text before answering, which adds delay and answer-parsing errors.
papers.fix: A model that picks the answer in one pass gained 7.93% accuracy and ran 6.04 times faster than the original.
papers.practicalUseCase: If direct answer scoring works, medical image tools reply much faster; skip text generation when choosing among set answers.
papers.limitation: Results come from four benchmarks and one 4B base model, with fixed candidate answers.
